newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end up before rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end up before rate decision.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Monday as investors waited for the Bank of Israel announcement on interest rates, traders said.
At the end of the trading day the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for January by 0.5 percentage point to an annualised 14.7 percent.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.83 percent, or 1.72 points, to 210.09 on all-share turnover of 98 million shekels against 80 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue-chip index gained 0.65 percent to 218.59.

"The session opened with nice gains and the market rose by more than one percent. Towards the end of the trading day we saw some profit-taking," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

"The market is rising very fast and in the next few days we must see a correction," said another trader. "But all the technical indicators are showing that the positive trend will continue after investors take profits."
"Everything looks good. The central bank was expected to lower the interest rate, the budget will be approved and it seems now that a deal over Hebron will be reached very soon," he added.
The market had expected a rate cut today of 0.3 to 0.5 point.

Palestinian officials reported progress on Monday in talks on an Israeli pullback from West Bank town of Hebron and said that U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross was trying to close a deal in time for Christmas.
Clal Israel, the main gainer on the Maof, rose 3.5 percent to 8,405 but traders said there was no evident reason for the rise.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which lost 0.75 percent to 28,355 on volume of 4.6 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which rose 1.0 percent to 452 on volume of 4.0 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 0.75 percent to 146,926 on turnover of 3.6 million shekels.
